To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NA stimulates adiponectin release in bovine adipocytes through a GPR109A-dependent pathway.
NA increased adiponeticin concentrations and the mRNA expression in bovine adipocytes, and that this effect was GPR109A dependent.
nicotinic acid increases adiponectin protein secretion and the mRNA expression for chemerin in differentiated bovine adipocytes through G-protein coupled receptors signaling.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new aspect of NA action in dairy cows, which could be of interest for dairy cattle nutrition.
the effects of NA in dairy cows, which is important for the understanding of the metabolic transition period.
the role of NA in the regulation of adiponectins and chemerin in bovine adipocytes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the G-protein-coupled receptor signaling pathway is important for the NA-induced adiponectin release and chemerin expression in bovine adipocytes.
NA increases the secretion of adipokines in dairy cows, which is mediated by GPR signaling.
NA stimulates the release of adiponectine in differentiated bovine adipocytes through GPR109A-dependent signaling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NA increases adiponectin concentration and chemerin mRNA abundance, and this is GPR109A-mediated.
NA increases adiponectin in vitro, possibly via GPR109A and/or chemerin signaling, and thus might improve insulin sensitivity and adipocyte metabolism in the dairy cow.
NA increases the secretion of adipokines in cattle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NA can be used to improve the insulin sensitivity and metabolism of bovine adipocytes.
NA may be a useful tool to modulate adiponectin in dairy cows.
NA may improve metabolic health by increasing adiponectin production in dairy cows.
